comparison.objective: Align a suction tool plate with a robot quick-change flange and actuate its locking ring so the tool remains suspended; the candidate sets and locks an internal gripper opening stop.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1054 tests carrying a tool, precise flange/dowel alignment, holding it seated, and operating a locking lever with the other hand. The candidate tests dual-tool coaxial seating and coordinated screw-versus-jam-nut countertorque, followed by operating a test lever.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1054 requires the correct tool seated and locked, the wrong tool never locked, hands clear, and arms returned; its versions specify dowel capture and ring-angle thresholds. The candidate requires a numeric opening angle, repeated retained motion, limited drift, hardware retention, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparison.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization during locking, but PR-1054 principally measures component alignment, insertion, and latch retention, while the candidate measures preservation of a calibrated rotational setting under tightening reaction and subsequent cycle stability.
